sentences.text: This dinosaur measured between five and six meters in total length, marking it as a creature of moderate size.
Its skull was distinctively shaped, reaching fifty-two centimeters in length and twenty centimeters in width across the eye sockets.
The mouth contained a mix of tooth types, with six teeth in the front upper jaw and thirty in the main upper jaw.
Scientists uncovered fossilized seeds trapped inside the rib cage of the main specimen, representing the first preserved meal ever found in a basal ornithischian dinosaur.
The larger seeds kept within the body showed three distinct layers: a fleshy outer coat, a hard middle shell, and an inner core.
Since the outer fleshy layer remained intact, researchers believe the animal swallowed these seeds whole rather than chewing them.
The remains were discovered in the Los Molles Formation of Patagonia, Argentina.
These fossils date back to approximately one hundred sixty-eight million years ago during the Bajocian stage.
Although it looked similar to stegosaurs, this animal lacked the famous bony plates and may have stood on two legs.
Analysis of the seed structures suggests they belonged to cycads from the family Zamiineae.
Based on its dental structure, it is possible that the creature had an omnivorous diet, though this remains a speculation since no animal bones were found with the seeds.
It is also possible that bacteria lived in its intestines to help break down tough plant material like seeds.
Isaberrysaura belongs to the class Ornithischia.
Initially, this dinosaur was placed in the Genasauria group at the base of the ornithischian family tree.
Salgado and colleagues noted that the animal possessed traits of both neornithischians and thyreophorans but did not fit neatly into either specific group.
The parent group for this species is identified as Huayangosauridae.
Consequently, Isaberrysaura is classified within the family Huayangosauridae.
Although initially thought to be a basal neornithischian, it is now allied with Stegosauria because its skull shape resembles other members of that group.
Several subsequent phylogenetic analyses have confidently classified Isaberrysaura as a stegosaur.
A later study by Han and others suggested that this species would be one of the most basal known members of the stegosaurs.
This animal lived during the Bajocian stage, a period between one hundred seventy point nine and one hundred sixty-eight point six million years ago.
While its teeth suggest an omnivorous diet, the absence of animal remains alongside seeds makes this conclusion speculative.
It is debated whether enzyme-producing bacteria were present in the gut to aid in digesting tough plant material like seeds.
